<!-- Generated by plugin-tools build-ports from commands/review.md. -->
Stage 5 (Review) for the change in `logic-fabric/.active`, or a review of the named artifacts: (the text the user gave after the skill's name)

1. Check `status.yaml`: `stage: review` (for a change). Outside a change, review what was named and skip the gates.
2. Hand the review to the `logic-fabric-dataverse:reviewer` agent (`logic_fabric_reviewer` in Codex) with: the project, the change folder, and the
   artifacts the change created or changed (from `build-log.md`). Don't pass it your own opinion of them.
3. If the change adds or changes a business process, also run `analyze` `kind: "process"` on it and hand the result
   to the `logic-fabric-dataverse:process-analyst` agent (`logic_fabric_process_analyst` in Codex). If it touches who can run what (preconditions, exposed
   tools, service connections, security), run `analyze` `kind: "security"` on the changed artifacts and hand it to
   the `logic-fabric-dataverse:security-reviewer` agent (`logic_fabric_security_reviewer` in Codex).
4. Merge their findings into `review.md` (template in the `authoring` skill), one row per finding with severity,
   artifact, path, rule, evidence and fix. Update `findings_*` in `status.yaml`.
5. Each blocker or major finding becomes a fix task in `plan.md` (`F-n`), unless the owner chooses to accept it as
   a risk (ask them; it stays `open` in `review.md`, with their reason in its Fix column). The build fixes them:
   offer it as a choice in your question tool (`/logic-fabric-dataverse:build`; "Offer the next step" in the
   authoring skill says how), then review again: only the changed artifacts, closing or reopening each finding. When every blocker and major finding is fixed or kept open by the owner's choice, send the change for
   acceptance through Foundry (`release`, `action: "submit"`, the `changeId`, `options.review` the full `review.md` as
   saved). Foundry records the review's findings; accepting the change then accepts the open ones as risks with the
   owner as their approver, and an open blocker needs a reviewer first. Foundry refuses `submit` while the change has
   an open blocking item: finish or close those tasks first (authoring skill). From then on Foundry makes no changes
   for it until the owner decides. Then set `stage: acceptance`. If Foundry answers that this environment doesn't keep
   the stages of changes, set the stage anyway and say so in `build-log.md`. Offer the next steps as choices in your
   question tool: commit the change folder and run the acceptance (`/logic-fabric-dataverse:accept`), only commit, or
   not now.
